claims: NASA currently projects the Artemis III mission to launch in 2027.
The Artemis II flight is scheduled for 2026.
The Artemis III mission follows the Artemis II flight.
Artemis III is designed to test critical rendezvous and docking capabilities in low Earth orbit with commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin.
Artemis III is designed to prepare for a subsequent crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV in 2028.
The Artemis III mission goal is to test new Extravehicular Activity (xEVA) suits in orbit.
The Artemis III mission goal is to test integrated life support in orbit.
The Artemis III mission goal is to test propulsion systems in orbit.
The Artemis III mission tests systems in orbit rather than an immediate lunar landing.
The Artemis III mission will utilize commercial landers.
The Artemis III mission partnerships include SpaceX (Starship HLS).
The Artemis III mission partnerships include Blue Origin.
The Artemis III crew will launch from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
The Artemis III crew will launch on the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The timeline for the Artemis III mission was updated in early 2026.
The Artemis III mission timeline was updated to focus on ensuring the readiness of essential technologies for long-term exploration.
